                                          Inchgower Finn Thomson Single Sherry Cask #2289 Whisky 17 Year Old · 2009 Vintage

                                          70cl · 44.8% ABV
                                          £89.95

                                          In stock

                                          HTFW Cat. No: LP26082

                                          Preview mode: simulated time active

                                          Loading delivery estimate

                                          Cask Strength Single Cask

                                          This Inchgower spent the majority of its maturation in a refill hogshead before being re-racked into a single Oloroso sherry cask in July 2024, where it gained an additional layer of richness and complexity without losing its distinctive identity.

                                          The spirit displays the wonderfully waxy texture for which Inchgower is so admired, complemented by an oily mouthfeel and a gentle peppery spice that gives the whisky its unmistakable individuality. While the distillery rarely enjoys the spotlight, careful maturation reveals a spirit of remarkable character, depth, and understated elegance.

                                          The Oloroso cask was selected to enhance rather than overshadow the distillery character. It contributes refined notes of dried fruits, toasted nuts, and subtle baking spice, bringing additional richness and complexity while allowing the spirit's natural waxy, coastal character to remain at the fore. The result is a beautifully balanced whisky in which spirit and cask exist in perfect harmony, each elevating the other without ever competing for attention.

                                          Discover Inchgower

                                          Discover More
                                          (INCH-gow-er) Inchgower was founded in 1871 by Alexander Wilson & Co. near Buckie, built to replace the earlier Tochineal distillery and using equipment from that site. Its history took an unusual turn in 1936 when Buckie Town Council bought the distillery after the company’s collapse, before selling it on to Arthur Bell & Sons in 1938. Bell’s later doubled capacity in 1966 by adding two more stills, and Inchgower now sits within Diageo’s portfolio.
